## The Hack

Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what analysts say is the biggest crypto hack ever. Attackers emptied Binance wallets on ten blockchains of about $6.3 billion in roughly 20 minutes on the night of October 29–30, 2026.

An initial investigation suggests "the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." The $6.3 billion Binance attack appears to be linked to a North Korean state-sponsored hacking group, according to TRM Labs.

## Impact on BNB Token

BNB fell 8–9% to about $690 overnight. However, that hack didn't result in any of its coin being lost.

## Binance's Response

Binance says it has resumed withdrawals following the theft of a record $6.3 billion in token assets from its hot wallets. Binance says it has restored backing for about 90% of the assets; that doesn't mean it has recovered 90% of the funds from the attacker. Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users.
